$comment: Layers 2 and 3 of four (ADR 0046). A `standard` namespace is somebody else's vocabulary and is recorded as a pointer, never copied: a copy goes stale without anybody noticing. A `vaulet` namespace is one nobody else has written down, and only there do we write name, kind and meaning ourselves. Layer 4 is an organisation's own namespace and is not listed here at all.

namespaces.note: Country and issuer extensions append a code, e.g. org.iso.18013.5.1.US. Includes family_name, given_name, birth_date, document_number, issuing_country, portrait, sex.

namespaces.defined_by: EU Digital Identity Wallet Architecture and Reference Framework — person identification data

namespaces.$comment: Written here because nobody else has. If a standard appears for it, this becomes a pointer and these names become aliases.
